parsed.rationale: All five members — `AppleMusicService`, `BandcampService`, `SoundCloudService`, `SpotifyService`, and `YouTubeMusicService` — are `type-alias-object` declarations in the same package (`MusicShareKit`) at structurally identical positions (line 13 in four of five files, line 21 in `SpotifyService.swift`), with `shared_field_count: 1` and no differing slots, indicating they share an identical structural shape. Because they are type aliases rather than concrete types, the most idiomatic Swift resolution is to introduce a unifying `MusicService` protocol (potentially a PAT if service-specific configuration types differ) that each concrete backing type conforms to, eliminating the parallel alias proliferation. None of the records carry any restraint markers (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all `false`), so no intentional-duplication rule applies. Introducing a shared protocol in `MusicShareKit` keeps all consumers within the existing dependency graph without adding a new package.
